title: Quick lows before 3.9.0
description: The last phase of 3.9.0: lows whose fix is small and needs no design decision. Each fix closes its class at a shared seam.
desiredOutcome: The quick, decision-free lows left after P163 and P164 are closed: report link decode, side-nav highlight, bugs-table chip wrap, Sort-select coverage, panel arrow a11y, STACK_BUDGET wording, three drive lows, a symlink spelling in start, a test marker.

findings.issue: Link validation is not at one seam: each FILTER_AXES entry's decode re-implements it by hand - five near-identical bodies `if (!offeredBy(<bar>, 'data-<x>').includes(h.<x>)) return false; <state> = h.<x>; return true;` plus bespoke area and date variants - and each re-spells the chip attribute its own `attrs` already declares (a third copy beside `attrs` and `paint`). The registry therefore holds the rule as an enumeration: a new axis whose decode omits the offeredBy call restores any value, and nothing in the code refuses it; only the browser gate's hr1 catches it, through a regex over the source spelling (finding 3). The task asked for the fix 'at the shared seam rather than per instance'.
findings.resolution: Declare what each axis's control offers once, in the entry (e.g. `offers: () => offeredBy(bar, entry.attrs[0], sel)`; search and the date pair declare their own acceptor), and have the one restore loop (exports.js `FILTER_AXES.forEach((axis) => { if (axis.decode(HASH)) ... })`) hand each decode only the HASH values its acceptor admits, so an unoffered value never reaches a decode by construction and the per-axis decodes shrink back to plain assignments. Keep hr1 as the browser-side proof.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Add a browser-gate case that clicks each side-nav entry at more than one width and reads that the highlight names the clicked section': sn1 excuses any entry the document ends before reaching the line and prints it as a note instead of judging it. Re-run on the new acme render: `note side-nav jumps the document ends before: 1512px #bugs (document ends 161px short)` - clicking Bugs at 1512px lights Ready (the end-of-document rule lights the last section), so the highlight does not name the clicked section and sn1 is green over it. The executor flagged this as a design call; the behaviour predates the diff (same on eed7a78b), but the gate as written does not read what the clause asked.
findings.resolution: Recommended: at the end of the document, let the section the reader jumped to (location.hash's target, when its top is on screen) win over 'light the last section', then delete the `short` carve-out so sn1 judges every entry. If the owner prefers the end rule, record that as a decision/fault and keep the note - but then the clause is narrowed by decision, not by the gate.

findings.issue: hr0 derives the link keys by spelling: `/\bkeys: \[([^\]]*)\]/` and `'([a-z]+)'` over the page source. An axis written `keys:['x']`, with a double-quoted key, or a key holding a digit or capital is silently not exercised, and hr0 only asserts HR_KEYS.length > 0, so a dropped key stays green.
findings.resolution: Cross-check the derivation against the registry's own shape: e.g. count the `decode:` members of FILTER_AXES in the source and require one keys match per entry (the empty `keys: []` of task-status included), or tolerate whitespace/quote variants in the regex and fail when an entry yields no match.

tasks.title: A report link restores only filters a control shows, and the side-nav highlights the section a jump lands on
tasks.description:
Two report behaviour lows, one class each, fixed at the shared seam rather than per instance.

1. A report link can restore a filter no control shows. Hash decode (the FILTER_AXES registry in plugins/audit/scripts/ui/report/page-state.js) accepts values no control offers and hides rows behind them with nothing pressed: `#!m=bogus`, `#!a=nosuch` (unknown model/area), `#!tev=constructor` (a prototype key), `#!from=notadate`, `#!au=nobody` (hides Usage rows). Separately `#!ps=done` is dropped without a word in the Active view. Fix: every axis's decode keeps only values its control offers (read off the control/DOM, own-property lookups only), and what it drops is not applied; the restored state is exactly what the controls show. Decide the ps-in-Active-view case so the user is not silently given a different filter than the link named (e.g. switch the View to one that shows it, or keep it as an honest no-op the counter states) - pick the least surprising, say why in the code comment. Add browser-gate cases in tools/check-report-interactive.mjs: per axis, a bogus value in the hash restores nothing hidden and nothing pressed; red-first them: the render committed at eed7a78b (git show eed7a78b:examples/acme-store/acme-store-audit.html) must fail the new cases; quote the failing lines.

2. The side-nav highlights the section above after a nav jump, at every width: a section's scroll-margin is --sp-2 while markSpy (page-state.js) treats a section as current only past the layers' height + 4px, so a jump lands just short of that line. Fix: derive both from ONE value (one source the CSS scroll-margin and markSpy both read), not two constants kept equal by hand. Add a browser-gate case that clicks each side-nav entry at more than one width and reads that the highlight names the clicked section; red-first it on the current committed render.

Refresh rendered followers (examples/report.sh, docs/demo-large.html via `python3 tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py --how`, `node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs`) so tests/test__refs.py and check-rendered-artifacts stay green. tasks.title: The drive's base-measure bound reads the red before asking, its documents say the bound, and a wait names a hand-out rather than a launch
tasks.description:
Three drive lows in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py and the documents that describe it.

1. In base_reading_for, the due-branch bound check (around the `unmeasurable_bound` call in the due branch) runs before the red's own reading is read. A `not-knowable` reading already names a base run (base_behind), and the decided-mark branch sends such a red to the writer; so once a start holds UNMEASURED_BOUND moved-code bases, a later not-knowable red gets a spurious `gate-red-base-unknown` ask whose sentence claims the base "could not be measured either". Fix: in the due branch check `unmeasurable_bound(before) and not base_behind(reading)` (read the reading first). Add a twin of the bi16 case in tests/test_drive_phase.py that goes red without the fix (prove it).

2. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (around the base-measure section, near "goes to the writer every time, bounded by the writer rounds") and the block comment above BASE_MEASURE_VERDICTS say an unrunnable red always goes to the writer. That stops being true once a start reaches UNMEASURED_BOUND moved-code bases (the due branch then stops every red of the start before it is measured). Add "until the start reaches the bound" (or equivalent) in both places, matching plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md which already says it correctly.

3. The `wait-gate` and the matching wait line for a phase gate say "the gate launched %(since)s has recorded no run for it yet", but the drive stamps that time when it HANDS OUT the run-test-gate step, not when a gate process starts - so the line asserts a launch it never observed. Fix the claim: word it as what the drive knows ("handed out at %(since)s; no run recorded since") everywhere this stamp is rendered, and keep the remedy rule. Update any test pins on the old wording.

Read writing-python, before-you-claim, no-silent-pass. No register ids in comments.

outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: (1) base_reading_for's due branch now reads the red's own reading before the bound stops it: past unmeasurable_bound, a reading that names a base run (base_behind) returns (None, reading, None) - decided by that reading, with nothing measured - and only a red with no base run gets bound_said's 'could not be measured either' stop. DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF'S LITERAL FIX: the brief said `if unmeasurable_bound(before) and not base_behind(reading)`, which falls through and launches a measurement (inline or background) for that red past the bound, breaking the bound's own contract ('no base run is launched for a red after it' in execute-task.md, 'BEFORE any measurement is launched' in the block comment). The mutation probe proves the literal form launches (bi17 red under it). Behaviour difference is narrow: the red goes to the writer on its own base-run reading, exactly as the decided-mark branch already sends it. (2) Block comment above BASE_MEASURE_VERDICTS and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: 'goes to the writer every time' now carries 'until the start reaches the bound', and both say a red whose reading names a base run is decided by it past the bound; the guide's 'goes to the writer as before' for a moved-code red got the same qualifier (same claim, same class). base_reading_for's docstring says the same. execute-task.md already said it correctly ('no base run is launched for a red after it') and is unchanged. tasks.title: start compares the plan directory and the project directory on one path resolution; a test marker is restored
tasks.description:
Two small manifest/test lows.

1. `audit-task.py start` counts the plan's own evidence as undeclared readers when the project directory is spelled through a symlink: the plan-directory exclude is computed from os.path.abspath(mpath), which resolves through the cwd's real path (/private/tmp/...), then taken relative to a --project-dir spelled /tmp/..., so the exclude comes out empty and ~20 files under docs/audit/evidence count as readers and start refuses. Fix: compare both sides on one resolution (os.path.realpath on both, or the module's existing canonical-path helper if one exists - search before adding). Look for the same abspath-vs-realpath mix elsewhere in the start/scope reader path and fix the class with one helper, not per call site. Add a case in tests/test_audit_task.py that builds a project under a symlinked directory and runs start through the symlinked spelling; prove it red without the fix (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp is one such link; build your own symlink under tempfile.mkdtemp() so it is portable, and skip with a printed reason on a platform without symlinks).

2. tests/test_usage_ledger.py has a section marker `# --- rx:the re-export` with the space after the colon dropped by an earlier edit; restore `# --- rx: the re-export`.

tasks.title: Chips and ids never break inside a word in any table, the Sort select is always in the matrix, and the stack-budget basis says only what it measured
tasks.description:
Three report layout lows, closed together because they share the layout matrix in tools/check-report-interactive.mjs.

1. The bugs table's STATUS chip wraps inside the word at 1440x900 ("Fixe / d", "Won' / t fix") and the ID column breaks "BUG- / 10". Fix in report-css/tables.css: chips and ids do not break inside a word (white-space: nowrap on the chip and id cells, or a min width from the longest chip - whichever keeps the table inside the page at the phone size). Widen the matrix's "no word split across lines" assertion (lm5) from the chrome to EVERY table's chips and ids (phases, tasks, bugs, ready-now, usage), so a table added later is covered by default; red-first it on the current committed acme render and quote the failing lines.

2. The Sort select in the phases table's head renders only when any phase is pinned (any_phase_pinned), and no committed fixture has a pinned phase, so the layout matrix never sees it. Add a pinned phase to the demo-large fixture's generator (tools/demo/gen-demo-manifest.py; re-render docs/demo-large.html via `python3 tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py --how`), and make the matrix FAIL by name on demo-large when no Sort select is present (a fixture that stops carrying it must not pass silently). Keep tests/test_gen_demo_manifest.py green and update its pins honestly.

3. Two wording fixes beside STACK_BUDGET (change no share): (a) the sentence saying a phone whose filter bar wraps one more row fails lm4 - the cheapest row measured is 27.4px against 27px of headroom and lm4's stack is a whole-pixel scan that can sit up to 1.5px off, so only the 32px arm (a row holding the count) is shown to fail; say exactly that; (b) the rule's "over the class's screen height" must read "over that size's height" - a class holds sizes with different heights and lm4 applies the share per size.

Refresh rendered followers (examples/report.sh, docs/demo-large.html, `node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs`) so tests/test__refs.py and check-rendered-artifacts stay green. Read writing-css, refactoring-the-assembled-ui, before-you-claim. No register ids in comments.
